text:
maria: Heads up, we got a customer report: streaming requests from their IoT gateway are frequently getting idle-closed right at the 60s mark and clients immediately reconnecting leading to duplicate short sessions.

henry: I think this is the same class of bug as the other reconnects but notable because the gateway uses HTTP/2 -> WS upgrade through our proxy and we might be losing resume headers during the upgrade.

alex: Edge dump from the gateway trace:
```
2026-03-20T12:00:00.000Z EDGE: send 101 upgrade upgrade-ctx=gw-09
2026-03-20T12:00:00.120Z EDGE: incoming handshake headers: sec-websocket-protocol=redwood-stream; x-client-id=gateway-09; # no x-resume-token
```

maria: For this tenant the sessions are low-token (<20 tokens) so billing impact is small but support is noisy.

henry: Quick fix ideas: (A) keep-alive pinging from edge for idle sessions (if no activity) to avoid server idle-close, (B) make runtime tolerate missing resume token if fingerprint + last seq id matches, (C) console collapse as previous threads discussed.

alex: (A) could increase cost on our side; (B) again has abuse vector. Maybe do (A) for small number of affected tenants as opt-in.

henry: Also add telemetry tag `upgrade_path=htt2-ws-proxied` to help filter. Right now we don't tag upgrade path in stream events.

maria: I'll coordinate with support and propose an SLA temporary adjustment for gateway customers.

ops-bot: Note: created alert rule stream_idle_close_rate > 0.4% for tenant group 'gateways'

deploy-bot: Plan: edge keepalive pilot -> Thurs 01:00 UTC, runtime tolerant-resume feature-flag behind tenant opt-in -> Mon 09:00 UTC.

henry: We'll also add a debug header logger for 24h to a couple affected tenant logs to verify header presence.

maria: Thanks. Let's triage at standup tomorrow and prioritize canary for the edge keepalive pilot.
